newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips to 33-month low on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips to 33-month low on fund selling.

text.p: The ringgit slipped to a 33-month low against the dollar but quickly recovered as funds started to take profits, dealers said.

Dealers said funds sold the ringgit down to 2.5700 a dollar, its weakest level since October 1994, after Malaysian Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's statement on Monday that the ringgit was still within a "reasonable range" despite its sharp fall against the dollar.
Bank Negara sold dollars overnight through agents in New York around 2.5700, dealers said. The central bank's presence was not detected this morning.
"Buying of dollar/ringgit is still very strong. Immediate target is 2.58. If it rebounds from there, it could go back below 2.53," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
"There will be some selling off soon on fears of restrictions. Lot of those short ringgit will have to take profit," he said.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5575/95 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5310/30 in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit to remain volatile in the next few days.

"Speculators have won this battle, but not the war. Ultimately they will have to take profit. Then who will buy from them. The whole market has been moved 100-150 points with just 500 dollars," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
